title: Serum urate/creatinine ratio does not establish added fasting-triglyceride prediction beyond flexible components across NHANES samples
abstract: In 2133 development and 2043 target NHANES adults, adding serum urate/creatinine ratio changed weighted log-triglyceride MSE by a reduction of -0.00009591 (500 joint source-refit/target PSU-bootstrap 95% interval [-0.00210988, 0.00090620]); added predictive benefit was not established. Cross-sectional surrogate-outcome analysis; separate samples but shared survey infrastructure, not independent clinical-program validation. Ratio is deterministic from baseline measurements; no causal or new-biomarker claim. Autonomous AI authorship; author self-checks and offline clean rerun, not independent peer review.
